articles.title: Marc Márquez explota como nadie los sábados
articles.standfirst: El de Ducati puede sellar de forma matemática su décima corona en el Sprint de Portimao. Precisamente en el formato corto es donde ha marcado más la diferencia en el curso 2026
articles.summary: El de Ducati puede sellar de forma matemática su décima corona en el Sprint de Portimao. Precisamente en el formato corto es donde ha marcado más la diferencia en el curso 2026
articles.body: La capacidad para sobreponerse a las dificultades es probablemente la virtud más decisiva de Marc Márquez para haber desnivelado la balanza. Pero existe otro factor que ha sido igualmente esencial para que el '93' cuente con su segunda bola de partido en Portimao. Y ese no es otro que la tremenda explosividad que luce los sábados. El de Cervera siempre ha sido muy consistente en las cronometradas (este año acumula 4 poles, pero a lo largo de su trayectoria atesora nada menos que 106). Y luego en el formato corto es el número 1 de la parrilla. A lo largo de su trayectoria, el corredor de Ducati ha conseguido ganar 25 carreras al sprint. Pero sus triunfos de este año son más valiosos porque en estas pruebas es donde más ha marcado la diferencia. A falta de dos rondas, Marc se ha apropiado de 10 victorias (Brasil, Jerez, Hungría, Alemania, Aragón, San Marino, Japón, Indonesia, Australia y Qatar) en las pruebas en las que se reparten menos puntos. Los otros dos candidatos al título están muy lejos de este guarismo. Jorge Martín se ha impuesto en cuatro y Marco Bezzecchi no ha conseguido ganar ni uno solo. Y si así se observa una enorme diferencia en cuanto a rendimiento en las carreras de los sábados, si nos atenemos a la puntuación global obtenida a lo largo de la campaña la brecha es incluso mayor. En los Sprint, el mayor de los Márquez atesora 164 puntos (de los 431 que figuran en su casillero, lo que supone un 38% de su producción). Mientras que Martinator suma 119 (de sus 371) y Bez lleva sólo 80 (de sus 357). Ahora mismo, en la clasificación general del certamen, Marc aventaja en 60 puntos al de San Sebastián de los Reyes y en 74 al de Rímini. Si miramos qué renta saca al binomio de la escudería de Noale con lo cosechado los sábados obtenemos lo siguiente: +45 con respecto al segundo y +84 con respecto al tercero. Precisamente, Marc cuenta con otro match-ball para sentenciar de forma matemática el campeonato en el próximo Sprint que se disputará en esa espectacular montaña rusa que es el circuito luso. Si el ilerdense conquista la victoria ya no tendrá que sacar más la calculadora. Habrá logrado su décima corona (la octava en la clase reina). Otra forma menos estruendosa de obtenerlo es sacar dos puntos a Martín. Necesita acabar la jornada con 62 de diferencia sobre el madrileño. Lo que es un hecho irrefutable es que el competidor de 33 años ha mostrado una mayor consistencia en los Sprint (10 victorias de 20 posibles, lo que arroja un 50% de efectividad) que en las carreras dominicales a lo largo de toda la temporada. De hecho, las pruebas cortas fueron las que le mantuvieron en la pelea por la corona hasta que besó el asfalto en Le Mans con dramáticas consecuencias. Eso sí, a partir de la ronda celebrada en Balaton Park, el nueve veces campeón del mundo empezó a destapar el tarro de las esencias en las citas donde se reparte un botín más cuantioso. Hasta siete victorias ha conquistado el ilerdense en los eventos estelares de cada gran premio frente a las seis de Bezzecchi y la única de Martín sellada en Francia. "Marc ha estado increíble, porque no ha cedido ni un ápice. Así que ahora sólo falta el último pasito y esperamos conseguirlo, porque creo que el Mundial cierra un capítulo importante de la era de MotoGP. Y cerrarlo como campeones del mundo sería algo aún más especial", resume, desde la más absoluta admiración, el probador ducatista Michele Pirro. Veremos si remata la faena en el Sprint de Portimao el justamente catalogado como Míster Sábado.

articles.title: McLaren chief Zak Brown says advice from Novak Djokovic will help F1 team bounce back from losing titles to Mercedes
articles.summary: Listen to Sky Sports' full length interview with McLaren chief Zak Brown on the latest episode of The F1 Show; watch the Las Vegas GP this weekend on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 4am on Saturday and the race at 4am on Sunday
articles.body:
Lando Norris was replaced as world champion by Kimi Antonelli at the Mexico City Grand Prix earlier this month before Mercedes sealed a dominant Constructors' Championship triumph a week later in Brazil.

McLaren won their first constructors' title in 26 years in 2024 before repeating the feat the following year, but a major change in the sport's regulations reset the pecking order ahead of the 2026 season.

Asked during a special episode of Sky Sports' The F1 Show about watching Mercedes celebrate on the podium after Norris had claimed something of a consolation victory for McLaren at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, Brown jokingly replied: "I just want to push them off and get our team back up there!

"I mean, first of all, congratulations to Mercedes and Kimi. Now I have an appreciation for how hard this is.

"And the sport is so competitive and the top four teams, I mean, to beat a Red Bull, beat a Mercedes, beat a Ferrari, you've got to be damn good.

"It just makes me want it more. We won 14 races last year.

"We've won three this year. Madrid, coulda, shoulda, woulda. So it's been a year that I feel like we've underperformed on the whole, but that's a learning. It makes us stronger.

"I think Brazil was awesome. That was McLaren at its best. The upgrades were great, the strategy, the drivers.

Brown then explained how tennis icon Djokovic, who has won a record 24 men's Grand Slam singles titles, previously gave him some advice that he and McLaren team principal Andrea Stella have taken on board as they prepare for the 2027 season.

"It's sport, and the big thing is, Novak Djokovic is a good friend of ours, and he's quite inspiring," Brown said. "When people say things to me, they stick with me, certain things.

"And he said, 'you can't control your emotions, how you feel is how you feel, but you can control how you react to them.'

"So, the emotions of not winning, as Andrea says, no poison biscuits, but you kind of sit back, take a deep breath, and you go, you know what, 'that's what happened, now let's go push forward and win.' And it makes winning feel so good."

'A lot of changes' to be made to 2027 McLaren

McLaren's relative struggles this season, during which Norris has still managed three wins with two races to go, were contributed to by the team pushing until the end of 2025 while others switched more focus to working on their 2026 cars.

There ended up being fundamental issues with the MCL40, such as a shorter wheelbase than some of their rivals, that made it difficult for them to consistently compete for wins.

Asked whether this was something that will be addressed on next year's challenger, Brown said: "Yeah, always addressing the race car.

"Weight was a big issue this year for a lot of cars, obviously a shorter wheelbase (results in a) lighter car.

"So yeah, I think there's things that, slow speed corners weren't great for us.

"We've learned a lot about the power unit this year, and deployment, and all the stuff that, we're all still learning.

"So yeah, I think this season, there's a lot of takeaways and changes we're going to make going into 2027."

Norris' superb victory at Interlagos saw the Brit continue his dominance over his team-mate Oscar Piastri this season.

After the pair were extremely closely matched last season as Norris edged out Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Piastri for the title, there has been a clear gap between them in 2026.

Norris is 94 points ahead of Piastri in the drivers' standings, has all three of McLaren's grand prix victories this season, and six podiums to Piastri's two.

There have been similarly surprising shifts in performance from last year to this year at other teams, with Antonelli outpacing George Russell at Mercedes and Lewis Hamilton proving far more competitive against his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc in the new cars.

Brown reflected: "I think we've seen it mix up a little bit of the grid, right? Charles last year got the better of Lewis. Lewis is getting the better of him. George got the better of Kimi, so I think it's mixed up the grid a little bit.

"I think if you look at Oscar's strengths, there were kind of big, brave corners. Now all of a sudden these new big, brave corners, it's like, 'hey lift, conserve, preserve.' So, I think there's a small element of him having to adapt to a new car.

"And then let's not take any credit away from Lando. I've never seen him drive better.

"So, I think you have a combination of Lando who's driving the best I've ever seen him drive. Oscar who's just not yet clicked with it. There's your gap, but it's not a big gap."

articles.title: Honda no aparece en la decoración de Aston Martin en Las Vegas, ¿cúal es motivo?
articles.standfirst: Casi todos los equipos presentan nuevas libreas en una de las carreras con más impacto visual del calendario
articles.summary: Casi todos los equipos presentan nuevas libreas en una de las carreras con más impacto visual del calendario
articles.body: Aston Martin es uno de los equipos, junto a Williams, que cambia su librea o decoración para el GP de Las Vegas que se corre el sábado noche en la ciudad de Nevada, aunque en España serán las 5.00 de la mañana del domingo. El escenario, el ser a la luz de los focos y debido a impacto publicitario que tiene, es una buena ocasión para ofrecer otra imagen en el circuito que transita por en famoso 'Strip'. En las imágenes ofrecidas por la escudería está llamando mucho la atención el hecho de que el logotipo y el nombre de Honda han desaparecido del coche de Alonso y Stroll para este fin de semana, donde pierda protagonismo el verde y aparece bastante blanco y algo de negro y azul. Habitualmente, el logo de Honda aparece en la parte trasera de la tapa del motor, junto al lado de pilar del alerón trasero y en la parte delantera, debajo del dorsal del piloto, pero en Las Vegas hay un pequeño cambio. Pese a las elucubraciones de los aficionados en redes, hay un motivo comercial evidente, que es la sustitución de Honda por el logo y el nombre de Acura, la división de lujo de la marca japonesa en Estados Unidos. De hecho fue el primer cambio de 'branding' de este tipo y la pionera en 1986, tras la cual Toyota haría lo mismo con Lexus poco después. Lo que sucede es que Acura quedó circunscrita al mercado americano y asiático, mientras Lexus (1989) o Infinity, perteneciente a Nissan (1988) si fueron luego implantadas en Europa. La de Las Vegas es una de las carreras que peor le van al actual motor japonés, algo ya anunciado por Alonso hace semanas. El motivo es que se trata de "un circuito en el que hay muchas rectas", que es el terreno en el que menos armas tiene el AMR26. "En el resto habrá oportunidades", comentaba Fernando después de conseguir el octavo en Sepang hace un mes y medio.

articles.title: Body of Melbourne Cup horse So You Are found in skip bin - 'Unacceptable and disrespectful'
articles.summary: REC Equine Specialists: 'After his death, So You Are was collected by our contracted service provider and taken to a licensed landfill. He should have been promptly and respectfully buried. What happened was unacceptable and disrespectful. We are deeply sorry'
articles.body:
The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper reported on Tuesday that racing stewards were investigating after a construction worker saw a dead horse in a skip bin at a waste centre and posted a video on Facebook.

Trainer Bjorn Baker had released a statement the previous day saying So You Are died following a severe bout of colic. The five-year-old gelding was rushed to a specialist equine hospital for emergency veterinary treatment but couldn't be saved.

Baker posted an update on Tuesday after discovering So You Are hadn't been properly buried.

"Like everyone who has seen the footage, I am deeply distressed by the handling of So You Are's remains," Baker said. "He was a much-loved horse, and he deserved to be treated with dignity and respect after his death."

So You Are placed eighth in the Melbourne Cup on November 3, with Point of Law winning the 166th running of the two-mile classic.

In a statement to news.com.au , REC Equine Specialists managing partner Dr Jonathan Lumsden said So You Are had been "humanely euthanised under anaesthesia" after receiving emergency treatment.

"After his death, So You Are was collected by our contracted service provider and taken to a licensed landfill. He should have been promptly and respectfully buried," Lumsden said.

"What happened was unacceptable and disrespectful to So You Are and to everyone who cared for him. We are deeply sorry."

Lumsden said he was working with the service provider and the state's horse racing authority, Racing NSW, to establish what happened and "to put in processes to ensure it never happens again".

"No owner should have to go through what So You Are's connections have experienced this week," he said.

Racing NSW said So You Are was awaiting burial when the video was recorded.

"The way in which So You Are's body was left is distressing and completely unacceptable," Racing NSW said in a statement. "So You Are deserved to be treated with dignity and respect."

The state's racing regulator said under industry guidelines, a licensed landfill was the preferred option for animals which have been euthanised because of the chemicals involved in the process.

"That burial, however, should have occurred in a timely and respectful manner," the statement continued. "If through the course of our ongoing investigation any wrongdoing is found, Racing NSW will not hesitate to take appropriate action."

articles.title: F1 Q&A: Bearman and Ferrari, Williams, Racing Bulls, overtaking and renaming of grands prix
articles.summary: BBC F1 correspondent Andrew Benson answers your latest questions before the Las Vegas Grand Prix.
articles.body:
The 2026 Formula 1 season closes with three races in consecutive weekends, the first of them a night race in Las Vegas.

With the drivers' and constructors' titles won by Kimi Antonelli and Mercedes respectively, there remains a close contest over who finishes second in the drivers' championship.

Before the race along the Vegas' Strip, BBC F1 correspondent Andrew Benson answers your latest questions.

Is Ollie Bearman's career in danger of stalling by being at Haas and stuck in the Ferrari bottleneck? He obviously has the talent to be a world championship contender but being stuck at the back of the grid can't be doing his career any good. - Dave

Oliver Bearman has still not been confirmed as a Haas driver for 2027, even though both parties say that's what they want.

From Bearman's point of view, it's not hard to see why he might be asking a few questions about his future.

He is a member of the Ferrari driver academy and they show no sign of wanting him not to be, but at the same time they are not showing much sign of wanting to promote him to the senior team.

In that sense, Bearman's future hangs to a degree on Lewis Hamilton's.

Hamilton is talking about staying in F1 at least until 2030, which would mean a new contract at the end of next year, presumably with Ferrari.

But will Ferrari keep him? That is unknown, amid what has undoubtedly been some tension between him, team-mate Charles Leclerc and the team management this season.

If Hamilton stays, Bearman would be within his rights to ask how they see his future, and to ask for the chance to look for opportunities elsewhere.

How secure is James Vowles' position at Williams? He seems like a great guy, always very open and honest. But the fact remains that the team targeted this year for a big performance jump and they've actually gone backwards. Is Vowles running out of time? - James

Williams have had a bad season in 2026. There is no question about that.

For three years since Vowles became team principal in 2023, he had been talking about 2026 as the team's opportunity to take a significant step towards their ambitions of returning to the front.

Having finished fifth in 2025 - a result that even surprised the team - another step forward was expected this year under the new rules.

But that's not what happened. Instead, Williams have gone significantly backwards.

The car was late, too heavy and lacked downforce. Little relative progress has been made through the year and they lie ninth in the constructors' championship with three races to go and will almost certainly finish there.

All year, Vowles has been explaining that the new rules exposed pressure points in the Williams factory that he had not realised existed. Essentially, the factory systems were not able to cope with the demands being put on them.

He says they needed this experience to be able to fix them and move forwards to a better place.

A critic might question why Vowles had not realised they were there in the three years he had been leading the time up to that point.

Drivers Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon have been unimpressed by what has happened this year.

But Vowles succeeded in getting both to stay on for at least one more season. Although whether that was because they retain belief in the team or because they did not have that many better options is a debatable point.

Asked what gave him the confidence to stay, Albon said: "This year I've been brought into a more deeper analysis of where it went wrong from last year to this year.

"So why were we late? Why was the car overweight? What were the reasons? Why did we miss the trick on even the philosophy of the car, for example?

"I'm satisfied with what those reasons are. As simple as that, really.

"At the same time, I also want to see these things materialise and I want to see these changes happen next year."

Albon admitted to there being a "deep frustration shared with the whole team that after all the efforts of prioritising this year's car, we haven't delivered a good job".

A new, lighter chassis was introduced at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. That will be carried over into next year so, as Albon puts it, "we start next year's car with a chassis that's not heavy, that's on the right foot, that we can then start focusing a lot more on not losing weight and a lot more time on aerodynamics and making the car go faster".

Through this season, Vowles has taken to publicly calling for a revision to the cost-cap rules, saying they bake in an advantage for the big teams, and wanting allowances for extra spending for others to catch up.

His critics say that those allowances are already there in one form, and that Vowles is using this as a distraction technique.

Whether his job is on the line if there is not a significant step forward for 2027 after all this is not clear. But the pressure is mounting, and he will certainly have a lot of explaining to do if there isn't.

With Max Verstappen established at Red Bull for the foreseeable future, what is Racing Bulls' real purpose: to discover Max MkII for Red Bull or simply provide a route to finding a reliable number two? Is it time Racing Bulls was allowed to operate as a genuinely independent, competitive team, rather than effectively functioning as Red Bull's driver development programme? - Michael

Racing Bulls' raison d'etre is the same as it has always been through all its name changes since Red Bull bought Minardi at the end of 2005.

That is to act as a training ground for drivers for the main Red Bull team.

It can be argued that the Red Bull young driver programme has not been especially successful.

In 20 years, the only top-line driver it has brought up through the junior categories all the way to being a success at Red Bull Racing was Daniel Ricciardo.

Sebastian Vettel was a BMW driver before Red Bull signed him, and Max Verstappen was plucked straight into F1 by Red Bull after winning a tug-of-war with Mercedes while he was in F3.

And Carlos Sainz had to leave the Red Bull programme to get his opportunity in a leading team in F1.

That's not a great track record in two decades of operation, and it's exactly why a new approach has been taken now Helmut Marko and Christian Horner are no longer involved.

In the past, you can pretty much bet that Liam Lawson would have been released this season and that Arvid Lindblad and Nikola Tsolov would be Racing Bulls' line-up in 2027.

Instead, Red Bull have kept Lawson on alongside Lindblad, and Tsolov will have to wait his turn.

The reasoning behind that was to be more systematic about driver evaluation.

On balance, Lawson has had the upper hand on Lindblad this season, even though the Briton has shown significant promise in his highlights in his rookie year.

After being dropped after two races in 2025, Lawson is highly unlikely to be given a full-time seat at Red Bull again.

So, the argument went, if Lindblad can't beat him, he shouldn't be promoted either. So Red Bull decided to give Lindblad a second season alongside Lawson to prove whether he can beat the New Zealander.

If he can, he might get a chance of promotion at some point. If he can't, then give Tsolov his chance.

Live commentary on BBC Radio 5 Live and 5 Sports Extra; live text updates on BBC Sport website and app

What is it about a circuit that makes it good for overtaking and why is it that some tracks seem to make overtakes so very difficult? - Ollie

The simplistic answer to this question is to provide a long straight with a hard braking point into a slow corner at the end of it.

In reality, it's a bit more complex than that, but there are certain tracks that give a decent blueprint.

Silverstone and Austin, for example, are two of the best tracks for racing on the calendar.

Both have the above, but they also include sequences of corners through which cars can follow each other, trying alternate lines for attack and defence.

Think the combination of corners from Turns 12 to 16 in Austin, for example. Or the run through Vale, Club, Abbey, Village, the Loop down the Wellington Straight and into Brooklands and Luffield at Silverstone.

Another good example is the run from Turn One to Turn Four at Bahrain - a long straight into a big braking zone, a combination of corners where a driver can get the switchback and then an open slow corner where overtaking is possible on either side.

At the same time, there are certain characteristics that militate against overtaking and good racing.

One is combined braking and turning on corner entry - a reason drivers cited for the lack of overtaking at the new Madrid circuit this year.

Another is negative-camber corners, which is why overtaking at Abu Dhabi has always been so difficult, as that track has a lot of them.

Since Abu Dhabi was revised a few years ago, racing has improved there because of two key changes.

One was to change the fiddly chicane section at the end of the second long straight into one long banked corner, Turn Nine. Lewis Hamilton and George Russell raced side by side through there in their final race as Mercedes team-mates in 2024

Another was to take out the chicane before what is now Turn Five and open up its entry and narrow the exit. That's to provide different lines under braking - similar to the uphill entry to Turn One in Austin.

Why are traditional geographical country race names being replaced by city-branded GPs, such as 'Sao Paolo' (formerly the Brazilian Grand Prix) and 'Mexico City' (formerly the Mexican Grand Prix). I feel a certain amount of heritage has been lost by F1 no longer calling these classic races by their country names. - Jordan

The naming of a grand prix is usually pretty simple - it's after the country in which it is held. But that's not always the case.

When it is not, the reason is usually to do with a mix of financial and promotional reasons, and that is the case for both Brazil and Mexico.

Naming them after the city rather than the country was a request from the organisers as a result of various issues to do with funding and support, as well as raising awareness of the cities through branding.

articles.title: Fernando Alonso: Aston Martin driver to race in Dakar Rally ahead of 2027 F1 season in return to rally-raid event
articles.summary: Aston Martin's F1 driver joins the marque's first foray into the hugely-challenging Dakar Rally in January; 2027 event being held in Portugal and Morocco; watch the Las Vegas GP this weekend on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 4am on Saturday and the race at 4am on Sunday
articles.body:
The 45-year-old will return to compete in the legendary off-road endurance event seven years on from his one previous appearance, when he finished 13th with Toyota.

That came during Alonso's two-year stint out of Formula 1 but this time he will race in Dakar ahead of what will be a record-extending 24th campaign in the sport after he extended his deal with Aston Martin's F1 team for the 2027 season.

The 2027 edition of the rally-raid event is being held in Portugal and Morocco on January 9-23 after being moved from Saudi Arabia due to the conflict in the Middle East. The race will feature a prologue and 12 different stages across different challenging terrains.

Alonso's co-driver will again be compatriot Marc Coma, who is a five-time Dakar motorcycle category winner, in one of three Aston Martin Dreadnoughts being built and run by Prodrive. Sebastien Loeb, the nine-time World Rally champion, and reigning World Rally Raid champion Lucas Moraes will drive the other Aston Martin Racing entries.

Alonso said: "After deciding to continue racing in Formula 1 with the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team, I thought carefully about Dakar.

"In the end, the decision became simple. I wanted to embrace the challenge completely and take on both Formula 1 and the Dakar Rally in the same year.

"In 2020, Dakar was one of the most challenging and enjoyable experiences of my career.

"I have enormous respect for this race and the specialists who have mastered it. Having Marc alongside me again is very important, and with Aston Martin, Prodrive, Sebastien and Lucas we have an exceptional team.

"Formula 1 remains my priority. But I am a racing driver, and challenges like this are why I love competing. I'm looking forward to seeing what we can achieve."

The Dreadnoughts will the competition-ready version of the car originally designed in digital form as a military vehicle for the new Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 video game

Aston Martin CEO Adrian Hallmark said: "Aston Martin Dreadnought was conceived to dominate any terrain, under the most extreme circumstances and come through it all to deliver on its mission. Now along with our engineering partner, Prodrive, we will challenge this vision in the most extreme competitive environment in global motorsport - the Dakar 2027.

"It is in Aston Martin's nature to forge forward with pioneering concepts, and just as we have always done, explore their limits on the global stage. We do not shy away from such challenges, but embrace them, and in Fernando, Sebastien and Lucas we have three great champions with whom to mount a formidable challenge on Dakar 2027."

The event covers a total distance of 7,824km, including 4,341km of special stages, and features all manner of challenging terrain and desert conditions

It begins in Loule, Faro in Portugal's Algarve with a prologue on January 9 and finishes in Marrakech, Morocco on January 23.

articles.title: Oficial: Fernando Alonso vuelve al Dakar en 2027 con Aston Martin
articles.standfirst: El equipo británico anuncia su presencia en la próxima edición con el asturiano, Sebastien Loeb y Lucas Moraes como alineación estelar
articles.summary: El equipo británico anuncia su presencia en la próxima edición con el asturiano, Sebastien Loeb y Lucas Moraes como alineación estelar
articles.body: Ya es oficial: Fernando Alonso será la estrella del Dakar 2027... y de su equipo: Aston Martin. El bicampeón mundial de Fórmula 1 disputará su segundo rally Dakar al volante del primer Aston Martin en la historia de la prueba. Así lo ha confirmado hoy la marca británica, que, además, ha anunciado la composición de su escuadra para la 49ª edición del rally más duro del mundo. Además de Fernando Alonso (que repetirá junto a Marc Coma como copiloto), lo formarán Sebastien Loeb (tal y como adelantó MARCA), que vuelve junto a Fabian Lurquin y Lucas Moraes, que tendrá a su lado a otro español, Pablo Moreno Huete (ex copiloto de Cristina Gutiérrez). También, confirmando lo anticipado por este medio, sabemos que el coche se llamará Aston Martin Dreadnought, el nombre del prototipo que creó la marca británica para el videojuego Call of Duty, cuyas formas se replicarán sobre la base mecánica del actual Dacia Sandrider, vigente ganador del Dakar en manos de Nasser Al-Attiyah (que, como también anticipamos, deja el equipo para marcharse a Ford). Será el segundo Dakar de un Fernando Alonso que se enamoró de la prueba tras su debut en la primera edición disputada en territorio saudí, en 2020. Desde entonces, el piloto asturiano siempre ha asegurado que volvería a disputarlo... aunque no se esperaba que lo hiciera en combinación con su carrera en F1 (recordemos que el asturiano ha renovado una temporada más con Aston Martin). De hecho, él mismo consideraba hasta hace apenas unas semanas que ambas disciplinas no podrían compatibilizarse: "No creo que el Dakar sea físicamente compatible con la Fórmula 1", dijo tras desvelarse que planeaba disputar el rally de nuevo, en los días previos al Gran Premio de Singapur de Fórmula 1. Alonso estará fantásticamente bien rodeado... pese a que ninguno de los tres pilotos del nuevo equipo Aston Martin sepa lo que es ganar un Dakar. Pero nadie duda de que todo un nueve veces campeón del mundo de rallies y cinco veces podio como Sebastien Loeb es un candidato claro a la victoria. Una carrera que se le resiste, pero que el francés tiene a su alcance, para lo cual volverá a recurrir al belga Fabian Lurquin en el puesto de copiloto, hasta ahora navegante de Nasser Al-Attiyah, con quien logró el triunfo en la última edición del Dakar. Lucas Moraes, por su parte, luce en su curriculum el título de campeón del mundo de rally raid que logró el año pasado con Toyota, justo antes de cambiar el volante del prototipo japonés por el competitivo Dacia Sandrider, con el que disputó el Dakar 2026. En su debut con el equipo francés (con el que no pudo correr ninguna carrera antes de tomar la salida en Arabia Saudí) el brasileño fue séptimo en la general, sin sumar victorias de etapa. Sin embargo, su potencial quedó demostrado desde su debut con Toyota, en 2023, en el que logró un espectacular tercer puesto. El coche que pilotará Fernando Alonso en el Dakar 2027 se construye sobre la misma base que el actual Dacia Sandrider, aún en competición (la próxima semana disputará su última carrera en la cita final del Mundial de Rally-Raid, el Abu Dhabi Desert Challenge, donde aún aspira al título con Al-Attiyah y Loeb). El coche fue desarrollado desde el principio por el especialista británico Prodrive, que seguirá al frente de las tareas de fabricación y operación de los ahora Aston Martin Dreadnought en el Dakar 2027. Carrera en la que debutarán, ya que la firma de Gaydon no ha tenido tiempo material de, siquiera, hacer un rally previo a la cita marroquí. Porque, de forma excepcional por el conflicto en Oriente Medio que sacude especialmente a Arabia Saudí, el Dakar 2027 deja el país asiático para volver a sus orígenes africanos, en concreto a Marruecos, que acogerá la gran mayoría del recorrido de la 49ª edición (que saldrá de Portugal el 9 de enero y concluirá en Marrakech el día 23). No será un terreno desconocido para Fernando Alonso y Marc Coma, que ya debutaron juntos precisamente en el Rally de Marruecos 2019 como preparación para su estreno dakariano. Además, el copiloto del asturiano tiene un curriculum excelso en esa carrera en su etapa en motos, donde se impuso en tres ediciones. El asturiano y el catalán se enfrentarán a 13 jornadas de competición (12 etapas más un prólogo) con un total de casi 8.000 kilómetros de recorrido de los que más de 4.300 serán de especiales cronometradas.

articles.title: Fernando Alonso explica por qué vuelve al Dakar: "Quería asumir el desafío por completo"
articles.standfirst: El asturiano, deseoso de afrontar el reto adicional de hacer un segundo Dakar "en el mismo año que la Fórmula 1"
articles.summary: El asturiano, deseoso de afrontar el reto adicional de hacer un segundo Dakar "en el mismo año que la Fórmula 1"
articles.body: Fernando Alonso empezará el año 2027 con un gran reto: volver al Rally Dakar. Será su segunda participación en el rally más duro del mundo, en este caso, además, compaginándolo con su faceta como piloto de Fórmula 1. El asturiano ha confirmado hoy su participación en la 49ª edición del Dakar junto a su equipo, Aston Martin, que debutará en la carrera que este año se disputará en Portugal y Marruecos. Alonso explicó cuál fue el 'timing' de su decisión de volver al rally-raid quizá antes de lo esperado, dado que su trayectoria en la F1 no ha terminado. “Tras decidir que seguiría compitiendo en Fórmula 1 con el equipo Aston Martin, reflexioné detenidamente sobre el Dakar”, señala. “Al final, la decisión fue sencilla: quería asumir el desafío por completo y disputar tanto la Fórmula 1 como el Rally Dakar en el mismo año". Algo que nadie ha hecho antes. En el caso de Alonso, pudo más el buen sabor de boca de su debut (en el que fue 13º y dejó destellos ): "En 2020, el Dakar fue una de las experiencias más exigentes y gratificantes de mi carrera. Siento un enorme respeto por esta prueba y por los especialistas que han logrado dominarla". Uno de esos es su copiloto, Marc Coma, que repite a la derecha del bicampeón en tareas de navegación: "Volver a tener a Marc a mi lado es muy importante y, junto con Aston Martin, Prodrive, Sébastien [Loeb] y Lucas [Moraes], contamos con un equipo excepcional". El francés y el brasileño también han sido confirmados por los de Silverstone para esta su primera aventura dakariana. Alonso afrontará su segundo Dakar con un feeling similar al del primero, como un reto gigantesco en una disciplina totalmente opuesta a la de su día a día: "La Fórmula 1 sigue siendo mi prioridad. Pero soy piloto, y desafíos como este son la razón por la que me apasiona competir. Estoy deseando ver lo que podemos conseguir”, concluye. El reto en el escaso mes y medio que queda hasta el arranque del Dakar 2027 (previsto para el 9 de enero en Faro, Portugal) es acumular más días de test -hasta el momento sólo ha podido completar tres días al volante de su nueva máquina-, algo que no será sencillo de conseguir puesto que ya no habrá respiro para los pilotos de F1 hasta que finalice la temporada, el próximo 6 de diciembre en Abu Dhabi.

articles.title: Ecclestone vuelve a atizar a Hamilton
articles.standfirst: "Es demasiado tarde", o "debe plantearse dejarlo", dice Bernie sobre el heptacampeón
articles.summary: "Es demasiado tarde", o "debe plantearse dejarlo", dice Bernie sobre el heptacampeón
articles.body: Bernie Ecclestone sigue en una actitud absolutamente crítica respecto a Lewis Hamilton, algo que lleva sucediendo desde el el británico anunció su fichaje por Ferrari y que se sigue repitiendo cíclicamente en el tiempo. Aunque el hecho viene de atrás, cuando el antiguo capo de la F1 fue eliminado como presidente de honor de la competición por una entrevista en la que vertía valoraciones que se parecían mucho a opiniones racistas. Hamilton le reprendió en 2020, tras aquellas declaraciones. Ahora el que fuera Supremo de la F1, que cumplió 96 años el pasado 28 de octubre, vuelve a la carga contra el heptacampeón. "Cuando se sube al coche para empezar una carrera, ya está quejándose y protestando por algo antes de la primera curva, sea lo que sea", ha dicho en Sky Alemania. "Está llegando a una edad en la que tiene que plantearse dejarlo". Además, no duda en elegir a Charles Leclerc como el piloto de futuro de la Scuderia. "Leclerc es un hombre de Ferrari, mientra Hamilton, en cambio, llegó e intentó cambiar la forma de trabajar del equipo. Ya es demasiado tarde para que lo consiga por sí solo", argumenta. El director del equipo Ferrari, Fred Vasseur, se vio obligado a mantener una reunión de reconciliación con sus pilotos en Brasil, tras el incidente ocurrido en la primera vuelta del Gran Premio de Ciudad de México y las duras críticas de Lewis contra el monegasco, en las que le acusó de ser agresivo contra él en carrera, mientras que no lo es con otros como le pasa con Verstappen.

articles.title: McLaren ya está a la altura de Mercedes: factura 744 millones, pese a volver a pérdidas en 2025
articles.standfirst: La escudería de Woking prácticamente ha duplicado ingresos en los últimos tres años para situarse en el podio de ingresos de la parrilla de F1
articles.summary: La escudería de Woking prácticamente ha duplicado ingresos en los últimos tres años para situarse en el podio de ingresos de la parrilla de F1
articles.body: McLaren F1 continúa acelerando su negocio impulsado por sus éxitos sobre el asfalto. La escudería británica se ha consolidado como la que más ha crecido en ingresos de la parrilla de la Fórmula 1 en los últimos años, aupada por una ambiciosa estrategia comercial que le ha llevado a crear un ecosistema de casi 60 marcas, en el que destaca Mastercard como title sponsor y marcas como Google, Cisco, DP World, Intel o Etihad entre sus patrocinadores oficiales. La escudería papaya elevó un 21% su facturación en 2025, hasta 621,2 millones de libras (744,4 millones de euros), según las cuentas anuales analizadas por Intelligence 2P, la unidad de estrategia e inteligencia de mercado de 2Playbook. Con este impulso, la estructura de Woking ha transformado sus buenos resultados deportivos (dos campeonatos del mundo de constructores y uno de pilotos incluidos) en una cifra de negocio más que relevante. De hecho, ya se ha consolidado en el podio del ranking de ingresos de la F1, solo por detrás de Ferrari y Mercedes, a la que ya casi iguala en facturación. McLaren completó la reordenación de su accionariado el pasado curso, después de que Mumtalakat y CYVN Holdings, un vehículo de inversión del gobierno de Abu Dhabi, se hicieran con el control total de la escudería. El fondo bahreiní posee el 70% de las acciones, mientras que el emiratí tiene cerca de un 30%. Con todo, la valoración de McLaren ya se sitúa en 6.300 millones de dólares (5.715 millones de euros) tras crecer un 33% en 2026, según Sportico. El incremento en la cifra de negocio de la escudería británica se atribuye principalmente al avance del negocio comercial. McLaren firmó en 2025 a Allwynn, Okta, Goldman Sachs, eBay, T-Mobile, Lego y Mastercard como patrocinadores oficiales. La compañía de servicios financieros elevó su posición de cara a 2026 como el primer naming partner de la escudería, que había dejado vacante este espacio desde la salida de Vodafone hace ya más de una década. Se calcula que Mastercard paga entre 90 millones y 100 millones de dólares anuales por este acuerdo. Esta temporada, otras de las novedades han sido la permuta de Castore a Puma como nuevo patrocinador técnico y la llegada de Etihad Airways como aerolínea oficial. A los ingresos por comercial se les suma un incremento más que relevante del prize money. Se calcula que la escudería percibió alrededor de 161 millones de dólares (146 millones de euros) en premios de la Fórmula 1 por su rendimiento deportivo en 2024, edición en la que se hizo con el Mundial de constructores 26 años después. La cifra irá a más el próximo curso cuando recoja los emolumentos percibidos por otra temporada récord en la que, además de otro Mundial de constructores, también hay que sumarle el Mundial de pilotos que cosechó Lando Norris. El principal retroceso que ha experimentado el equipo dirigido por Zak Brown está en el resultado neto. La estructura británica volvió a números rojos tres años después, con unas pérdidas de 17,4 millones de libras (20,8 millones de euros). La escudería aprovechó para pagar algunos de los préstamos que recibió durante la Covid-19, cuando afrontó sus mayores dificultades financieras. El equipo venía de obtener unas ganancias de 54,2 millones de libras (64,94 millones de euros) en 2024 y otros 12,9 millones de libras (15,4 millones de euros) en 2023. La compañía había vuelto al positivo ese año tras perder 188,6 millones de libras (226 millones de euros) desde 2019. Anteriormente, la venta de su fábrica en Woking le había reportado unas ganancias récord de 85 millones de libras en el 2020. Más gasto en salarios y bonus de casi 100 millones para Brown La estructura de Woking también elevó los costes un 37,4% interanual, principalmente por el aumento de los pagos al personal. De hecho, la estructura es líder en gasto en salarios de la parrilla tras más que duplicar su inversión en personal en solo dos años. El coste en plantilla pasó de 134,9 millones de libras (161,6 millones de euros) en 2023 a 285,6 millones de libras (342,2 millones de euros) en 2025, y creció un 72,8% interanual. Cabe destacar que la plantilla alcanzó los 1.246 empleados, por los 1.123 del ejercicio anterior. Las cuentas también desgranan los emolumentos que percibió Zak Brown como principal responsable de la escudería. El directivo recibió una compensación de 81,9 millones de libras (98,14 millones de euros) que incluía tanto su salario base, de 8,2 millones de libras, como un pago de incentivos en la temporada en la que el equipo se proclamó campeón de pilotos y constructores, valorado en 73,7 millones de libras. Este plan estaba vinculado a la reestructuración corporativa que supuso la entrada del fondo de Abu Dhabi, CYVN Holdings, en el accionariado. Por otro lado, McLaren ha diversificado este año más allá de las pistas con el lanzamiento de su vertical de golf McLaren Golf. Se trata de la primera vez que la estructura de Woking se adentra en el mundo del golf y se encargará de la fabricación y comercialización de equipamiento de golf.

articles.title: Melbourne Cup Horse So You Are Found Dead in a Waste Facility, Sparking an Inquiry
articles.summary: SYDNEY (AP) — The dead body of Melbourne Cup horse So You Are was found in a waste facility in Sydney less than two weeks after competing in the most prestigious event in Australian horse racing.
articles.body:
SYDNEY (AP) — The dead body of Melbourne Cup horse So You Are was found in a waste facility in Sydney less than two weeks after competing in the most prestigious event in Australian horse racing.

The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper reported Tuesday that racing stewards were investigating after a construction worker saw a dead horse in a dumpster at a licensed waste center and posted a video on Facebook.

Trainer Bjorn Baker had released a statement Monday saying So You Are died following a severe bout of colic. The 5-year-old gelding was rushed to a specialist equine hospital for emergency veterinary treatment but couldn't be saved.

Baker posted an update Tuesday after discovering So You Are hadn't been properly buried.

"Like everyone who has seen the footage, I am deeply distressed by the handling of So You Are's remains," Baker said in a statement. "He was a much-loved horse, and he deserved to be treated with dignity and respect after his death."

So You Are placed eighth in the Melbourne Cup on Nov. 3, with Point of Law winning the 166th running of the 2-mile classic.

REC Equine Specialists managing partner Dr. Jonathan Lumsden issued a statement saying So You Are had been "humanely euthanized under anesthesia" after receiving emergency treatment.

"After his death, So You Are was collected by our contracted service provider and taken to a licensed landfill. He should have been promptly and respectfully buried," Lumsden said. "What happened was unacceptable and disrespectful to So You Are and to everyone who cared for him. We are deeply sorry."

Lumsden said he was working with the service provider and the state's horse racing authority, Racing NSW, to establish what went wrong and to put in processes to ensure it never happens again.

"So You Are was in our care. We did not carry out the burial ourselves, but we chose the provider and the arrangements, and we take full responsibility for that," he said. "We should have known exactly how horses were handled after leaving our hospital, and we did not. That process is not good enough, and it must change.

"No owner should have to go through what So You Are's connections have experienced this week."

Racing NSW said So You Are was being held temporarily, awaiting burial, when the video was recorded.

"These images are distressing for all involved and for all of us who care deeply about our horses," Racing NSW said in a statement. "The way in which So You Are's body was left is distressing and completely unacceptable. So You Are deserved to be treated with dignity and respect."

The state's racing regulator said under industry guidelines — now under review — a licensed landfill was the preferred option for animals which have been euthanized because of the chemicals involved in the process.

"That burial, however, should have occurred in a timely and respectful manner," the statement continued. "If through the course of our ongoing investigation any wrongdoing is found, Racing NSW will not hesitate to take appropriate action."

articles.title: NASCAR’s TV Numbers Hit A New Low Despite $1.1 Billion Deal
articles.summary: NASCAR viewership dropped 2% to an all-time low in 2026. New talks with Skydance might fix the problem, but the numbers tell a scary story.
articles.body:
The numbers are in, and they are not kind to NASCAR. The 2026 Cup Series season averaged 2.419 million viewers, a 2% drop from 2025 and the lowest average in series history, according to Sports Business Journal . The decline comes despite NASCAR's current media-rights agreements, reportedly worth approximately $1.1 billion annually through 2031. The sport is facing a difficult question: how can it reverse its declining television audience while navigating an increasingly fragmented media landscape?

Kyle Larson won his third title on Sunday, but the final race at Homestead-Miami drew only 2.5 million viewers. That figure marks the lowest championship audience in at least a decade, per the Sports Business Journal . The decline is sharp when you look back just seven years. The last time the finale ran at Homestead in 2019, NBC averaged 3.74 million viewers. That is a massive gap for a sport trying to grow its brand.

Fragmentation is killing the ratings. Most races now air on cable channels where fewer people can find them. The cable portion of the 2026 schedule, which included 24 races, averaged 1.94 million viewers, down 5% from 2025, according to Yahoo Sports. Even worse, the five least-watched races of the year all aired on USA Network. The fall race at Phoenix Raceway ended last with only 1.294 million viewers.

USA Network averaged approximately 1.6 million viewers for its Cup Series races, a 4% decline from 2025. The network's first five races were actually up 3%, but its final five, which coincided with college football and NFL games, fell 11%. Football competition appears to have contributed to the decline, particularly during the fall schedule. Broadcast TV still performs better, but the shift away from open channels is clear. Broadcast races averaged 3.57 million viewers, down 4% from last year.

NASCAR may have an opportunity to bring some races back to broadcast television. Skydance completed its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery in October, bringing TNT Sports and CBS under the same corporate umbrella. NASCAR CEO Steve O'Donnell has discussed the possibility of moving races currently scheduled for TNT to CBS. NASCAR EVP Brian Herbst also confirmed that conversations with Skydance have begun. Any changes, however, remain under discussion.

Herbst also noted that NASCAR is trying to find its place among other major sports. Herbst stated, "What I try to think about is [NASCAR's] position in the sports landscape," pointing to similar figures seen in other major sports properties. The 2.4-million average is on par with the NBA regular season, but the trend is worrying. The league needs to act fast before the gap widens further.

articles.standfirst: El de Gresini está listo para volver en Portimao, después de haberse perdido la cita de Qatar
articles.summary: El de Gresini está listo para volver en Portimao, después de haberse perdido la cita de Qatar
articles.body: En Qatar no estuvo un Álex Márquez que decidió pasar por el quirófano tras la celebración del Gran Premio de Malasia de MotoGP. El competidor de Gresini necesitaba solucionar sus problemas en el hombro derecho. Recordemos que el '73' sufrió un escalofriante accidente en Montmeló durante la carrera dominical y, a partir de ese preciso momento, no consiguió estar a tope físicamente hasta que ha decidido poner fin a su calvario. Sea como fuere, el octavo clasificado en el certamen (con 197 puntos) ya está listo para regresar antes de que caiga el telón de una temporada 2026 con muchos giros inesperados. El de Cervera será de la partida en esa montaña rusa que es el trazado luso, tal y como han confirmado el propio piloto y su escudería. "Tras dos semanas de duro trabajo es hora de volver a la competición. Nos vemos en Portimao", ha subrayado, a través de las redes sociales, el que fuera subcampeón de la clase reina el curso pretérito. El ilerdense, que debutará con la KTM RC16 en el test de postemporada de Valencia el próximo 1 de diciembre, no ha podido brillar con tanta intensidad este año como lo hiciera en 2025. El motivo principal no es otro que el hándicap físico mencionado que le ha hecho perderse hasta cuatro rondas (Italia, Hungría, República Checa y Qatar) de la campaña que está a punto de extinguirse. Eso sí, al '73' le queda el consuelo de haberse impuesto en la prueba larga disputada en Jerez y en el Sprint del Gran Premio de Cataluña. La otra gran novedad para este fin de semana de carreras en Portugal, en clave Ducati, es que Iker Lecuona sustituirá al lesionado Pecco Bagnaia. El subcampeón del WorldSBK 2026 formará una duplamente totalmente española junto a Marc Márquez, quien cuenta con muchas opciones de conquistar su décimo título en el Autódromo Internacional del Algarve.

articles.title: Mercedes confirm ADUO turbo upgrade ready for Las Vegas GP with Kimi Antonelli set to run new engine part
articles.summary: Silver Arrows expecting to run ADUO update on Kimi Antonelli's car only as use of another turbo for George Russell would trigger fresh grid drop; watch the Las Vegas GP this weekend on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 4am on Saturday and the race at 4am on Sunday
articles.body:
Mercedes in June were granted one chance to upgrade their power unit this season after being found to be between two and four per cent behind the best-performing internal combustion engine - which was unexpectedly judged to be Red Bull's - by the FIA in the year's first ADUO (Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities) assessment window.

While rivals Ferrari, Audi and Honda, who were all found to be more than four per cent behind Red Bull's output and granted two upgrade opportunities, have all updated their respective power units at least once since, Mercedes had continued to keep their sole update chance in reserve.

But that ADUO upgrade - which Mercedes have focused on their power unit's turbo - is now ready to use in Las Vegas, although the team have played down the significance of its likely performance.

Given that expectation, Mercedes say that only world champion Kimi Antonelli is expected to use it given the Italian, who clinched the drivers' title two races ago in Mexico, remains one turbo within his penalty-free allowance of the season.

Russell has already used five turbos, one more than is permitted, due to unreliability earlier in the year and a sixth would trigger a further five-place grid penalty. The Briton, who dropped five places on the Sao Paulo Grand Prix grid due to an engine change, is in a five-way battle to finish runner-up to Antonelli in the standings with three races to go.

"We will have the ADUO enabled turbo specification available from this weekend," confirmed team principal Toto Wolff in Mercedes' pre-race preview.

"This is primarily about proving out the development in race-weekend conditions, with the expected performance benefit relatively small.

"We anticipate running it with Kimi, whilst with George our priority is protecting his grid position with the performance benefit likely too limited to justify taking a grid penalty."

Mercedes keen to help Russell finish 2026 in second

As Wolff said after Mercedes wrapped up the Constructors' Championship last time out in Brazil to go with Antonelli's drivers' crown from the week before in Mexico City, helping Russell finish second in the standings is now a priority for the team over the season's final three events.

Russell is currently third in the standings, 17 points behind Red Bull's Max Verstappen and only one point ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton. Charles Leclerc, Hamilton's Ferrari team-mate, and McLaren's Lando Norris are also not out of the running for second place yet either.

Wolff added: "Winning both world championships was an incredible achievement and we have taken the time to celebrate that.

"There is still plenty we want to achieve this season though, and now it is back to work. Our targets are clear: helping George finish as high as possible in the Drivers' Championship, ending the year with momentum, and continuing to unlock more performance from the car.

"There is more work to do on that front, and the final three races give us three more opportunities to learn and improve."

Mercedes have won 12 races this season but only one of those has come in the last five rounds with the challenge having grown during the year from Ferrari, Red Bull and McLaren.

The Silver Arrows were the dominant winners of the second Las Vegas GP in 2024 and Wolff admitted: "We know what it feels like to win there and we would certainly like to experience that again."

articles.title: Old Park Star, Sober Glory and Baron Noir clash at Ffos Las
articles.summary: Having been declared to clash at Cheltenham over the weekend, Old Park Star and Sober Glory both swerved commitments at Prestbury Park in favour of more suitable conditions in South Wales on Wednesday, and we are treated to a fascinating contest with Baron Noir also thrown into the mix.
articles.body:
You always need a bit of luck in this game, no matter what your role or ability. While the elements have unfortunately conspired against those at Exeter so far this season, Ffos Las is the beneficiary of what they are calling The Welsh Arkle on Wednesday, live on Sky Sports Racing .

The race got a huge boost with the somewhat surprise addition of 2026 Supreme Novices' Hurdle winner Old Park Star , a high-profile non-runner on Cheltenham's Saturday card due to the ground being deemed too quick. His inclusion means we have a huge early season clash with an old foe in Sober Glory , last season's unlucky Supreme runner-up.

The inclusion of Old Park Star is no doubt bad luck for those connected to Sober Glory et al; after all, the Henderson-trained horse was meant to run last Saturday, but it's a huge stroke of luck for Ffos Las and indeed, Sky Sports Racing. Exciting early season clashes like this are incredibly rare for novice chasers in Britain - and in general given the monster that the Cheltenham Festival has morphed into - so it's understandable there is a bit of a buzz around the industry ahead of the five-runner Golwg Gwendraeth Beginners' Chase , due off at 13:18pm.

As of 8.37am on Tuesday, on the back of 16mm since 6pm on Monday, the ground is officially Good (good to soft in places), but with significant rain due. According to the BHA site, tomorrow's forecast reads as, 'blustery with persistent rain, heavy at times throughout the day'. Hopefully it leads to beautiful soft ground which the horses will get through nicely.

As the official ratings and betting suggests, Old Park Star (155; 4/6) and Sober Glory (153; 15/8) are the standouts and are set to renew their rivalry having served up a fantastic Cheltenham Festival curtain raiser in March, along with Mydaddypaddy back in third. At the line, the winning margins were 1½ lengths and a nose, with the also reopposing Baron Noir (146; 10/1), Wednesday's third favourite, a further 6 lengths back in fourth.

Wednesday's prices and a glance at the formbook in black and white could lead you down the garden path of just siding the unbeaten hurdler Old Park Star, but replaying the final flight of their Supreme clash is wise, given it had such a significant impact on the race.

Heading to the last in the Supreme, Sober Glory looked to have everything in trouble with a good 1½+ lengths lead before he put in an extra stride, hit the hurdle and landed steeply, losing critical momentum. It was a huge shame for his connections because up to that point he had jumped so well and looked the best horse in the race going to the last.

That mistake cost him dearly, along with many punters having been a huge gamble from 16/1 in the morning to an SP of 9/2. The Philip Hobbs & Johnson White yard clearly felt like they had their charge in great order, produced him beautifully on the day only for that famous last flight on the Old Course at Prestbury Park to scupper a dream start to the 2026 Festival.

His disappointing run 31 days later at Aintree is easily excused on the back of a long season after a huge Cheltenham run and now with his attentions turned to chasing, this former Irish point-to-point winner for Cormac Doyle rates an exciting prospect for the upcoming campaign for owners Brocade Racing.

Standing in his way again is fellow six-year-old Old Park Star , who, to be fair, didn't exactly ping the final flight in the Supreme himself, also putting in an extra stride which led to the son of Well Chosen landing awkwardly but crucially, not losing as much momentum as Sober Glory.

That saw him stay unbeaten in four hurdle starts, after wins at Kempton, Cheltenham and Haydock, showing good versatility in terms of the tracks he could handle along with also displaying tactical adaptability. Having jumped right in places on debut, his hurdling got better and slicker as the campaign progressed and he looked a straight-forward character throughout.

Having been put away after Cheltenham, Old Park Star's attentions now to turn chasing, a game he possesses the physical scope and athleticism for, although unlike Sober Glory he has no point-to-point background. While not ideal, it's possibly a good sign that Nicky Henderson was willing to pitch him into Grade 2 company at Cheltenham on chasing debut before the ground ruled him out.

A horse said to be big and weak last season, there could be much more to come from Old Park Star, his trainer's comments of ' he's still a shell of a horse' last year continually playing on my mind. If he was able to achieve what he did last season when weak, you cannot but be excited about him after another summer on his back.

Baron Noir is certainly no no-hoper against Old Park Star and Sober Glory, with 7½ lengths and 6 lengths, respectively, to find with the leading pair, especially if he has settled down for a summer's break and/or fences curb his keen-going ways.

It's in his breeding to be highly-strung, being by Vadamos out of a Dylan Thomas mare, but he's a horse with plenty of ability and it was a clear sign of the belief his trainer Alan King had in him to run in a Supreme when only rated 130.

While essentially well-held at the line, the six-year-old shaped better than the distance beaten, not getting up the hill as well as his Wednesday rivals. With that in mind, the much flatter nature of Ffos Las should suit.

He too has no point-to-point background, but with the King yard ticking along nicely, he is certainly worth a market check.

It's not often you would get prices of 33/1 about a Grade 2-winning novice hurdler from the Skelton yard who looks all-over a chaser on novice chase debut, but that's the task facing Carlenrig . His odds are not just about the horses he is taking on, but also the trip, mind.

A winner of the Grade 2 Bristol Novices' Hurdle at Cheltenham last December, he showed a good attitude to win over that 3m trip. On the back of that given his unexposed nature, he looked a big player in the River Don Novices' Hurdle at Doncaster 42 days later - despite carrying a penalty - but having been a stinking drifter (4/1 out to 14/1), fell two out when his race looked to be run.

The former winning Irish pointer picked up a small injury that day and hasn't been seen in 298 days so this looks like a starting point to get his campaign up and running.

Stablemate Bobby's Nelson has his first run for the Skeltons and should be more at home over this 2m trip. He also looks a chaser physically and his three-quarter of a length defeat to Baron Noir last December at Uttoxeter doesn't half look bad now; indeed, you could argue he is overpriced at 80/1 on that effort, but is probably best watched.

In truth, this looks a race to watch for the future, but if forced to have a bet, at the prices, it would certainly be SOBER GLORY . I don't think it's far fetched to say he looked the best horse in the Supreme before his final flight mistake, and with his point-to-point background, might have a jumping experience edge over Old Park Star . That said, the Hobbs and White yard are only operating at a 5% strike-rate currently, for all they've had plenty of others run well. Either way, I am very much looking forward to seeing how all these horses take to fences.

articles.title: Nico de Boinville given extra security at Plumpton racecourse after threat
articles.summary: Jockey Nico de Boinville is given extra security support at Plumpton racecourse after being the subject of a threat.
articles.body:
Jockey Nico de Boinville had to be given extra security support at Plumpton racecourse after being the subject of a threat.

De Boinville finished fifth aboard the Nicky Henderson-trained Ginolo in the first race on Monday at the East Sussex track.

The 37-year-old was then told he would require additional security after officials were made aware of a threat to the Henderson yard.

De Boinville, who finished third on his only other ride at the track, suspected the threat transpired because he did not win on Ginolo.

"I need to find out a bit more about it, but it's the trials and tribulations of being a jockey," he told Racing HQ on Tuesday.

"I just feel sorry for whoever it was and I hope they get the help they need - it was probably because I got beat.

"It is bizarre and I'm going to work like everyone else and you don't expect that when you go to work."

A British Horseracing Authority spokesperson added: "The BHA condemns all abusive or threatening behaviour towards our participants, who rightly should expect to be able to go about their jobs without being subjected to anything of this kind.

"We work closely with our colleagues across racing's representative bodies and, where appropriate, will take whatever action necessary to ensure the safety of everyone in our sport."

articles.title: Nico de Boinville 'escorted to his vehicle' and given security support after threat received
articles.summary: Top jockey Nico de Boinville was racing at Plumpton and finished fifth in the opening race of the afternoon, before finishing third on his only other ride; he was given additional security protection throughout the day after a threat had been made to Nicky Henderson's yard
articles.body:
The multiple Grade One-wining jockey finished fifth aboard even-money favourite Ginolo for his boss Nicky Henderson in the opening race of the afternoon at the East Sussex track, after which he was informed he would be provided with extra security after officials became aware of the situation.

De Boinville went on to finish third on his only other ride, the Henderson-trained Ionian in a handicap chase, the third race on the card.

Explaining the sequence of events, Plumpton's clerk of the course Marcus Waters said: "We got a phone call from a person representing the PJA (Professional Jockeys Association) and the NTF (National Trainers Federation) regarding a threat that had gone in to the Henderson yard.

"We put on security for Nico for the rest of the day. He had one further ride and they escorted him from the weighing room to the parade ring and then once the race was done they escorted him to his vehicle, just in case there was anything that came with the threat.

"It's obviously not a nice situation for anyone to be involved with."

Speaking to Racing HQ at Newbury's pre-Coral Gold Cup gallops morning on Tuesday, De Boinville explained: "After the first race yesterday the security detail at Plumpton who are very good, top-level people who dealt with the Brighton bombings and things like that, came in and dragged me out and said there's been a threat called in to me, so I needed security for the rest of the day.

"The threat came into the yard and then the PJA and then BHA, and then it gets called through to the racecourse. I need to find out a bit more about it but it's the trials and tribulations of being a jockey.

"It is bizarre and I'm going to work like everyone else and you don't expect that when you go to work. I just feel sorry for whoever it was and I hope they get the help they need - it was probably because I got beat."

articles.title: Un Jorge Martín más entero en busca de lo imposible: "Llego a Portugal en mucha mejor forma física"
articles.standfirst: El de Aprilia saldrá al ataque en Portimao con el claro objetivo de evitar que Marc Márquez cante el alirón en la penúltima cita del calendario de MotoGP 2026
articles.summary: El de Aprilia saldrá al ataque en Portimao con el claro objetivo de evitar que Marc Márquez cante el alirón en la penúltima cita del calendario de MotoGP 2026
articles.body: Jorge Martín tiene prácticamente imposible evitar que Marc Márquez vuelva a entonar el alirón. De hecho, el ilerdense puede sellar de manera matemática su décima corona en el Sprint del Gran Premio de Portugal. Ahora mismo, el ‘93’ goza de una generosa renta: aventaja en 60 puntos a Martinator y en 74 a Marco Bezzecchi. ¿Qué necesita el de San Sebastián de los Reyes para llevar al límite (es decir, que el certamen se decida en Valencia) al mayor de los Márquez? Pues planteado de forma sencilla: necesita meterle 24 puntos a Marc a lo largo del fin de semana de carreras en Portimao. Lo tiene complicado por todo. En primera instancia, debería busca el pleno de victorias... y sólo ha sumado 37 puntos de una tacada este año en el evento disputado en Le Mans (Francia). Al menos, en el formato Sprint se ha mostrado más incisivo (cuatro triunfos) que en las carreras dominicales (sólo ha ganado una en lo que va de curso). El lado bueno de las cosas para el de Aprilia es que con vistas a esta penúltima cita del calendario del Mundial de MotoGP comparecerá en mejores condiciones de salud. Recordemos que en el Sprint de Phillip Island se fue al suelo con dramáticas consecuencias para sus intereses. No pudo competir en Sepang, pero acto seguido obró el milagro en Qatar (tercero en la prueba corta y séptimo en el evento principal). “Estoy listo para las dos últimas semanas del campeonato. Llego a Portugal en mucha mejor forma física y quiero dar lo mejor de mí con Aprilia y con todo mi equipo”, pormenoriza un Martinator que ha tenido que pasar por un duro proceso de rehabilitación desde que hace casi un mes sufriera una fractura en el radio distal de la mano derecha. “Tengo muchas ganas de correr en Portimao, es una pista que me gusta”, apostilla el ‘89’ en la previa difundida por la casa de Noale. En su discurso deja entrever que está dispuesto a morir matando. Sabe que no le queda otra que salir al ataque. Aparte de lo que se juegan de forma individual, la dupla de Aprilia pelea por lograr otros objetivos importantes a nivel colectivo. Será difícil que destronen a Marc, pero sí tienen a tiro el Mundial de Constructores. Ahí sí que albergan más posibilidades de salir victoriosos. Ducati domina con sólo 8 puntos de ventaja sobre el conjunto que encabeza Massimo Rivola (569 frente a 561). Por equipos, Aprilia saca 124 puntos (728 Vs. 604) a la escuadra oficial de la firma de Borgo Panigale.

articles.title: Casa de Saúde Santa Fé: Servidores contestam municipalização | G1
articles.standfirst: Abaixo-assinado tenta reverter processo de transição da unidade para o município; servidores relatam redução de atendimentos, enquanto prefeitura afirma que serviços serão mantidos e ampliados em Três Corações.
articles.summary: Servidores da Casa de Saúde Santa Fé em Três Corações iniciam abaixo-assinado contra a municipalização da unidade, alegando queda na qualidade dos atendimentos.
articles.body:
O processo de municipalização da Casa de Saúde Santa Fé, em Três Corações , tem gerado resistência entre servidores da unidade. Um abaixo-assinado virtual foi criado para tentar reverter a transferência da gestão para o município e manter a administração sob responsabilidade da Fundação Hospitalar do Estado de Minas Gerais (Fhemig).

A Casa de Saúde Santa Fé, que no passado foi referência em curativos e no tratamento de doenças de pele, atualmente tem atendimentos reduzidos, segundo servidores da instituição. Eles afirmam que apenas alguns exames são realizados na unidade.

Em dezembro de 2024, a gestão da instituição passou da Fhemig para o Consórcio Intermunicipal de Saúde do Circuito das Águas. Na época, o secretário de Estado de Saúde de Minas Gerais, Fábio Bacheretti, afirmou, em entrevista à EPTV , que a mudança tinha como objetivo reduzir filas e ampliar os serviços prestados.

"Vamos ajudar com equipamentos para que este hospital funcione melhor e vamos financiar e custear as cirurgias aditivas", disse o secretário em 12 de dezembro de 2024.

Servidores contestam municipalização da Casa de Saúde Santa Fé e pedem manutenção da gestão pela Fhemig — Foto: Reprodução EPTV

Segundo servidores, a ampliação dos atendimentos anunciada não ocorreu.

"Foi proposto ser um hospital dia, só que não está funcionando como deveria. Então foi proposto aquelas cirurgias eletivas de pequeno porte, que são cirurgias oftálmicas, entre outras. Então não está acontecendo isso", afirmou a técnica de farmácia da Fhemig, Gilzene Mariano Pigozzo.

O complexo de saúde Santa Fé atende uma região formada por pelo menos 50 cidades. Atualmente, diferentes serviços são oferecidos por meio de parceria entre a Fhemig e a Prefeitura de Três Corações.

Em junho deste ano, os servidores foram informados de que todo o complexo passará por um processo de municipalização. Com isso, os serviços oferecidos pela unidade ficarão sob responsabilidade exclusiva do município. O processo já está em andamento e tem prazo para conclusão em 31 de dezembro do próximo ano.

A principal preocupação dos servidores é a capacidade financeira e estrutural do município para assumir integralmente os atendimentos. Segundo Gilzene Mariano Pigozzo, alguns serviços já enfrentam dificuldades.

"Na questão do CER 4, o que é o CER 4? É Centro de Reabilitação Física. Não tem equipe multidisciplinar, não tem terapeuta ocupacional para atender essas pessoas. Tem famílias que ficam na fila aguardando esses tratamentos e não tem. Então, já está uma situação de gestão comprometida", disse.

Para tentar barrar a municipalização, servidores iniciaram um abaixo-assinado virtual.

A bioquímica da Fhemig Angela Mari Santos, servidora da fundação há 15 anos, afirma que o laboratório onde trabalhava foi desativado e que ela precisou ser realocada para outra unidade do complexo.

"A impressão que dá é que, assim, acabou o Hansenianos, acabou o serviço de saúde aqui. O tratamento de hanseníase aqui tem tudo para ser de atenção secundária e a gente está vendo que até a atenção primária acabou", afirmou.

De acordo com a Prefeitura de Três Corações, os gastos anuais com a saúde no município chegam a R$ 130 milhões, incluindo as despesas relacionadas ao complexo Santa Fé.

O secretário municipal de Saúde, Rachid Gadbem, afirmou que os serviços atualmente oferecidos serão mantidos e ampliados. Segundo ele, a municipalização também permitirá economia com aluguéis de prédios públicos, já que diversas especialidades passaram a funcionar na instituição.

"80% dos serviços já é do município, então viu-se por bem o município poder ampliar esse serviço de saúde. Então, além de ampliar ali, o governo do estado ampliou outras redes de serviço relacionadas até à municipalização, como equipamentos da nova UPA 24 horas, reforma de todas as unidades da atenção primária do município, troca de equipamentos. Então, está dando um aporte na saúde municipal e, consequentemente, da micro região como um todo. Então, a gestão municipal, a gestão de saúde do município viu que seria uma guinada jamais vista na saúde de Três Corações", disse.

O secretário também garantiu a permanência dos idosos que vivem na enfermaria da unidade. Entre eles estão João e Antônio, que demonstraram preocupação com o futuro da instituição.

"Para nós que moramos aqui, nóis é muito bem cuidado, graças a Deus. Está na cara que isso aqui vai acabar fechando. Isso não tem sentido, não", afirmou o pensionista Antônio de Paula Silva.

Em nota, a Fhemig informou que a municipalização da unidade integra a política da Secretaria de Estado de Saúde de Minas Gerais de reorganização do Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS), com o objetivo de aproximar, ampliar e qualificar a assistência prestada à população de Três Corações e região.

A fundação também destacou que a iniciativa segue o modelo federativo do SUS, no qual cada ente assume as responsabilidades de sua competência e passa a contar com as condições necessárias para exercê-las.

articles.title: ¿Y si Ferrari tentara a Antonelli?
articles.standfirst: Toto Wolff habla de esa posibilidad y tiene una respuesta muy clara
articles.summary: Toto Wolff habla de esa posibilidad y tiene una respuesta muy clara
articles.body: Una de las cuestiones más repetidas en los días anteriores y posteriores al título Mundial de Kimi Antonelli en México fue el motivo por el que la nueva estrella italiana no está pilotando hoy para Ferrari y el momento en el que fue rechazado por la Scuderia cuando sólo tenía 11 años y su padre logró que le hicieran una prueba en el simulador de Maranello. La respuesta, al parecer, que era muy menudo o muy niño todavía, es algo que debe suceder cientos de veces en las academias de pilotos de las grandes escuadras de F1. Fue Nico Rosberg quien lo de dio un volante en su academia de karting con 12 años y quien luego se lo presentó a Toto Wolff, quien sí vio el potencial. Con 16 años lo subió a la F2 sin pasar por la F2, con 18 le dio el Mercedes de Hamilton y con 19 empezó su segunda temporada, la de la corona. Después de su primer Mundial se ha debatido el hecho de que Ferrari querría tenerlo en sus filas en el futuro, para aunar la figura del primer campeón italiano en 73 años y el tercero de la historia, al icono del 'cavallino' como un posible binomio imbatible para los 'tifosi', sin tener que dividir sus preferencias como sucedió en Monza este año. Y a Toto Wolff se le ha cuestionado sobre una opción a la que nadie se ha resistido a lo largo de la historia, con Hamilton como último ejemplo de alguien que considera pilotar de rojo como gran colofón a su trayectoria. Para CEO de Mercedes la respuesta es tajante: "0,0 por ciento", ha respondido en una entrevista en 'Bild'. "Porque Kimi y su familia son personas leales", apostillaba. "En este caso, estoy convencido, sí. Pero no nos basamos únicamente en la lealtad. Esta temporada ha demostrado que podemos ganar carreras y títulos y eso es lo más importante para cualquier piloto, incluido Kimi. Él pertenece a Mercedes como las ruedas pertenecen a un coche", decía en una metáfora muy ilustrativa. "Por eso, tras ganar el título, (Antonelli) dijo que no se imagina pilotando para ningún otro equipo que no sea Mercedes", explicaba Toto para amarrar el razonamiento. Toto incluso cree que Antonelli podría llegar a ser más popular en Italia como piloto de Mercedes que Michael Schumacher con sus cinco títulos de rojo (2000-2004): "¡Por supuesto! Al fin y al cabo, es italiano", asegura. "Lo que Kimi ha logrado gracias a su naturalidad y éxito es que Italia, si bien sigue siendo una apasionada de su equipo nacional, Ferrari, también ha abierto sus corazones y almas a este pequeño italiano. Los 'tifosi' ahora visten camisetas de Ferrari con gorras de Mercedes", argumentaba. "Monza fue el ejemplo perfecto. Los espectadores se sintieron decepcionados de que ninguno de los dos coches rojos terminara primero, pero estaban encantados de que Kimi, uno de los suyos, estuviera en lo más alto del podio", señala. Cabe reflexionar sobre si Antonelli hubiera llegado a ser campeón en 2026 con Ferrari y la respuesta parece clara para casi todos. Nadie, salvo quizá Verstappen o Alonso (como ya hizo en su día) hubieran estado es disposición de luchar por el Mundial de pilotos hasta el final con el SF-26. Hamilton ha logrado una pole y una victoria y Leclerc un triunfo y quitando la lucha entre ambos en ese mes de junio, el coche no ha estado cerca de entablar rivalidad con Mercedes después de Silverstone en julio y eso es evidente. La falta de presión en el primer año de Kimi en Mercedes y la confianza ciega de Toto y el resto del equipo le dieron un ambiente en el que desarrollarse y eso en Ferrari hubiera sido casi imposible, o eso opina la mayoría, incluido el piloto y su familia.
